utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, can you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. Today is Monday. I would like to greet the accused who are present in the courtroom, the attorneys, the representatives of the OTP, as well as all the people assisting us in the courtroom. I shall first of all give the floor to our registrar who has five IC numbers to give us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Some parties have submitted lists of documents to be tendered through Witness Bandic, Ivan. The list submitted by 2D shall be given Exhibit IC955. The list committed by 3D shall be given Exhibit IC956, the list submitted by 4D shall be given Exhibit IC957, the list committed by 5D shall be given Exhibit IC958, and the list submitted by the Prosecution shall be given Exhibit IC959. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have two housekeeping matters to inform you about. First of all, on the 24th of March, i.e., tomorrow, there is a Plenary Session that starts at 12.30 and runs until half past 2.00. As far as I'm concerned, and this concerns my colleagues also, we wish to attend this Plenary Session which starts tomorrow at 12.30. Towards the end of the week, we have been advised by the Dutch authorities that on the 31st of March a conference on Afghanistan is to be held in The Hague, so in light of security issues relating to the attendees, there will be no hearing next Tuesday on the 31st of March. On looking at the schedule, I realise that Milos Mario was planned for two hours, so if everyone sticks to his or her time we will be able to get Milos Mario on Monday, the 30th of March, and finish with this witness on the 1st of April. The witness will therefore have to wait for 24 hours. On the 1st and 2nd of April, we have two witnesses who are scheduled who are due to testify for an hour. So there will be no hearing on the 31st of March, because the whole area around the World Forum will be cordoned off for security reasons. So we will not be able to get inside the Tribunal. This is what I wanted to share with you. Mr. Stringer, I believe you have something to tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, and good afternoon, Mr. President, thank you. Good afternoon to Your Honours, counsel. Mr. President, I need to make a couple of comments for the Trial Chamber and for the Defence as well with respect to my cross-examination -- or part of my cross-examination last week of Ivan Bandic, and I want to draw the Trial Chamber's attention to an exhibit that I used at the beginning of my cross-examination, P03630. This was the document that was used insofar as it related to a transfer of someone named Kasim Karhimanovic from Dubrovnik to Neum in July of 1993 and then to Dretelj; whereas, the document indicated he was beaten to death. And as -- as Your Honours may recall, there was a reference to the witness, Mr. Bandic, that I put to him in order to challenge his credibility at the time. The document had been admitted into evidence in this case in September of 2007. It was used during the direct examination of Witness DD earlier in February of 2007. Mr. President, before I decided to use the document in my cross-examination of Mr. Bandic, I asked that we do a little more investigation about the document on the issue of Mr. Karhimanovic, because I wanted to be assured that it was -- would be appropriate to put to Mr. Bandic given the gravity of the incident that is referred to there, and so we did do some additional looking into that document before we used it on the cross-examination, and we found in fact that there was documentation here within the Office of the Prosecutor that related to Mr. Karhimanovic as having been a member of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that he'd been transferred down to the Split logistics centre, and that he went missing in March of 1993. We also obtained a witness statement from 1994, that was given in 1994, by one of the sons of Mr. Karhimanovic who also talked about his father having been ordered to report to the police station in Dubrovnik in July 1993 and then was taken away and had never been seen again. So after we got that additional information, I elected to use the document on cross-examination of Mr. Banic. And then based on comments that Mr. Bandic made the following morning when he returned to testify, and then also some comments made by Mr. Coric when he intervened at a later point during Mr. Bandic's testimony, we renewed our efforts and did additional information -- or additional investigation into the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's all very interesting, and I do apologise profusely to my learned friend, perhaps before we get even more into the detail and the backgrounds of all these efforts made by the Prosecution, if we can have some indication as to what it is that my learned friend is seeking, and then, of course, the explanation can be understood. But I wonder if we could cut to the chase and find out what is it he's asking for at this moment in time and that would allow us to know whether or not this history as to the witness who was released last week, all of this is relevant or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Khan, let Mr. Stringer finish. Please proceed, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We continued to investigate. Mr. Coric had indicated that he thought the document had been used by the Prosecution in an interview. He was right. It turned out the document had been used by the Prosecution in a suspect interview of Mr. Kraljevic who was one of the purported authors of the document. And essentially, we determined that the document had been obtained by the Office of the Prosecution from the HVO archive in Zagreb on two different occasions and that this resulted in the document being given two different ERN numbers for processing. We determined that one version of the document was shown to Mr. Kraljevic during a suspect interview that was conducted by the Office of the Prosecutor on the 16th of November, 2004, and unfortunately that version had the different ERN number from the version that we have marked as Exhibit P3630, and that's why we didn't pick up the document earlier as having been used in the Kraljevic suspect interview when we did our checks beforehand. During the suspect interview, Mr. Kraljevic said this about the document, he said quote -- I'm quoting: "There was not Buntic's or my stamp." The court may recall that Mr. Buntic as one of the purported authors of the document. And then Kraljevic continued: "Then certain things here are exaggerated and certain persons protecting and there are false information." And then he continues. He says: "This was planted by the security service." And as I said, because the version that he was looking at had the different ERN number, even though it's the same document, we did not become aware of that prior to the cross-examination of Mr. Bandic. I found out this just as his examination was ending on Thursday. So although there is in our view substantial corroboration of much of the information that's contained in 3630, particularly or especially related to the arrest and the detention of Mr. Karhimanovic at Dretelj in July of 1993, we don't have documents that corroborate any role of Mr. Bandic in requesting that Mr. Karhimanovic be brought to Bosnia from Croatia, and for that reason, in light of the statement by Mr. Kraljevic about the document and in light of the gravity of the allegation regarding Mr. Bandic's alleged involvement in the incident, had I been aware of Mr. Kraljevic's statement in advance, I would not have used the document in my cross-examination of Mr. Bandic and would not have put that issue to him. And so as a result of this, the Prosecution would make two proposals to the Trial Chamber. First of all, we propose to submit to the Trial Chamber, and obviously copies to the parties as well, all of the information, the additional information and documentation that we obtained or that we identified in our checking of the document in order -- and including the excerpt, the relevant excerpt of the suspect interview of Mr. Kraljevic so that all of that information can be put before the Trial Chamber so that it can consider all of that in its assessment of the weight to be given to Exhibit P3630. We'd also propose, Mr. President, that in assessing the credibility of the witness, Mr. Bandic, that the Trial Chamber should not consider the reference to him that is contained in Exhibit 3630; that is to say, that while it may wish to consider Exhibit 3630 as relevant to other issues in the case, the Prosecution proposes that the Trial Chamber disregard Exhibit P03630 in determining the credibility of Mr. Bandic as a witness. So I apologise for the length of my remarks, Mr. President, but we wanted to bring this issue to the Trial Chamber's attention. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Khan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Khan, you see, there's no use in getting to your feet too quickly. Always wait for the other people to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, yes and no. This application could quite easily have been properly framed. It is a Prosecution application, in effect, under Rule 68, to discharge its functions in relation to exculpatory evidence or to at least clarify the record, and I'm very grateful to my learned friend acting with diligence and complete probity in bringing this Your Honours' attention. Your Honours, I've seen the proposal of my learned friend. It seems to be the sensible way of proceeding in light of the information that has come to light or that the Prosecution has become cognisant of since the witness concluded his evidence, but the only reason I did rise earlier is it's always useful when a narrative commences to know where it's going to finish, and this could all have been -- this was, of course, an application in some sense at least under Rule 68, and I'm grateful to my learned friend and of course the Prosecution as always.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall turn to my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] I apologise. It's not a Rule 68 application. In -- the suspect interview of Mr. Kraljevic was disclosed to the Defence previously. So the information about the exhibit, Mr. Kraljevic's statement about it, was disclosed previously. So it's something that we just wished to bring to the Trial Chamber's attention nonetheless.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stringer, the Bench accepts that you give us all the evidence you have discussed during your arguments. We will therefore be able to assess the probative value of the document in question. Mr. Usher, could you bring the witness into the courtroom, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: If I may add a consideration, Mr. Stringer. I do not think that this already indicates that we admit this documentation as evidence. You would have -- in case you would want that to -- to make an application to that effect. We'll just take it as information at the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I think that on this, Mr. President, we're in the Trial Chamber's hands. The Defence can look at the documentation, they can express their views, and the Trial Chamber can accept it or not as it wishes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wanted to thank the Prosecutor, and I believe that this is a good show of the efforts that were made in this particular case, and we commend the Prosecution, in particular Mr. Stringer, for his efforts. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd just like to say on behalf of the Petkovic Defence that I agree to what Mr. Karnavas has said, and I consider that this is an exceptionally fair gesture on the part of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, could you stand, please. Please give me your first name, last name, and date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Andjelko Makar. My date of birth is the 22nd of May, 1948.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your current occupation? What job do you have at the moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do different things, but I'm a retired general otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, have you already testified before court of law, whether it be domestic or international on those facts that unfolded in the former Yugoslavia, or are you testifying for the first time today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President, this is the first time I'm testifying to these facts, but I have testified in other cases before different courts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do you mean, a court in Bosnia, in Croatia, in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Different courts. Municipal courts, cantonal courts, and the Supreme Court and Constitutional Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I was at all those courts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please read the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some information I'd like to give you which I'm sure has been imparted to you by Ms. Nozica over the weekend. You will have to answer those questions that will be put to you by Ms. Nozica. Ms. Nozica is the Defence counsel of Mr. Stojic only, and therefore the other Defence counsel may put questions to you also as part of their cross-examination. The Prosecutor, who is on your right-hand side, I believe it will be Ms. West, will also questions to you as part of their cross-examination. The Bench before you may put questions to you also. Generally, we put questions based on the documents we have before us. I'm sure that Ms. Nozica and/or the Prosecutor will show you a number of documents. So please be as accurate as you possibly can when you answer this question. I'm sure as a former general that you will answer those questions in a cursory and accurate manner. Don't hesitate to have a question rephrased if you don't understand it. We have 20-minute breaks every hour and a half, but if at any point in time you wish to have a short break, please don't hesitate to let us know and raise your hand. You have taken the oath a few moments ago. Therefore, you are no longer a witness of one of the parties. You are now a witness of the court, which means that you may not have any contact anymore whatsoever with Mr. Stojic's Defence counsel. Ms. Nozica, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everybody else in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And good afternoon to you, Mr. Makar.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, before I start with my questions, I'm going to give basic information from your CV, which are important for this testimony of yours. Mr. Makar, you went to the military academy for the armed forces of the JNA in Belgrade from 1966 -- I apologise, 1967 to 1971.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: From 1971 until 1985, you were an active officer in the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You left the Yugoslav People's Army on the 13th of May, 1992, by reporting to the district staff of the Territorial Defence of Tuzla where you were appointed chief of communications in the staff; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In September 1992, after the 2nd Corps of the BH army was established in Tuzla, you were the assistant -- performed the function of assistant Chief of Staff for operations and training; right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: On the 18th of July, 1993, you were appointed Chief of Staff of the 2nd Corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And you remained in that post until the 25th of December, 1994, when you were appointed the deputy commander of the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And you performed different functions within the army of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and you did so until the 31st of March, 2000, when you retired.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, I'm going to ask you some introductory questions about how the war in Tuzla began, where Tuzla is located, how the defence was organise in the Tuzla region, so general facts to show where you come from and what happened in that area during the war? Now, could you please explain to the Trial Chamber when the conflict started in the Tuzla area and who provoked them?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the conflicts in the Tuzla area started soon after a referendum that was held with respect to the independence of the State of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and, more specifically, in the broader area of the Tuzla district. The conflicts began on the 8th of March with an attack by the Yugoslav People's Army and Serbian paramilitaries on Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, these conflicts with the JNA and the paramilitary Serbian forces, how long did they go on for in the Tuzla area?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: I would like to make a correction. The Yugoslav Army. It was no longer the Yugoslav People's Army, so just the Yugoslav Army, and conflicts in the area went on until the end of the war or, let's say, the signing of the Dayton Accords.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, and how was the defence of the Tuzla area organised after the first clashes and conflicts or immediately prior to them breaking out?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: The Your Honours, the defence of the Tuzla region was organised in the District Staff of the Territorial Defence, and under their command were 13 Territorial Defence Staffs of the municipalities. At the beginning, smaller units of the Territorial Defence were formed, and later on they grew into bigger units so that already in May and June of 1992 we had brigades. Later on, to cut the story short, at the end of 1992, in September, the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina took a decision to establish five corps. One of those corps was the corps in Tuzla, which was the 2nd Corps, and with the formation of the corps all the forces of the Territorial Defence, as well as the HVO forces in the area, were included and were subordinate to the corps. At the time, we had eight operative groups in the corps, and let me explain, Your Honours. An operative group is a military formation of the rank of a division, and those eight operative groups, of which I'd just like to mention Operative Group 1, had the 107th HVO Brigade and the 108th HVO Brigade and the 21st Brigade of the BH army. They all came under that Operative Group 1. Yes, I will do my best to slow down. Operative Group 5, Tuzla, had the 1st, 2nd, 3rd Tuzla Brigade of the BH army within its ranks, and the 115th Brigade of the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two short follow-up questions. On the 8th of March, 1992, where were you, you yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 8th of March, 1992, I was in Tuzla, and it was the 17th Corps of the Yugoslav Army at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Second follow-up question: If I understand correctly, the fifth group in Tuzla, in September 1992, brings together the 115th Brigade of the HVO and part of a brigade of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, Judge, you're quite right. There were three brigades of the BH army and one brigade, the 115th, of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which means that from March to September 1992, in Sarajevo, President Izetbegovic knows that in Tuzla there is an armed force that is made up of two elements, the HVO and the brigade of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, to clarify, you have just said that Operative Group 5 in Tuzla had within its composition three brigades of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and one HVO Brigade.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'd like to go back for a moment to Operative Group 1. You mentioned the 107th, which was also an HVO brigade.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You mentioned the 107th and 108th Brigades of the HVO. Would you tell us where these brigades were from so that we could have a clearer picture later on when we speak about them?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the 107th Brigade of the HVO was established on the territory of a town called Gradacac. When it was formed, it was called the MHVO, which means the Muslim Croatian Defence Council. The 108th Brigade of the HVO was established on the territory of Brcko, in the area of the town of Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, were there other operative groups which included HVO brigades when the 2nd Corps was formed?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, to continue where I left off, after Operative Group 5 we also had Operative Group 7 which was on the territory of the municipalities of Maglaj, Tesanj, Zepce, and that Operative Group included the 201st, the 202nd, the 203rd, and the 204th brigades of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and the 110th Brigade of the HVO which was also known as the Usora Brigade. To go back for a moment, Operative Group 2 on the territory of Gracanica-Doboj also had within its composition a brigade of the BH Army and the 109th HVO Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, please explain to Their Honours how the HVO was established in the Tuzla area?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: The HVO on the territory of Tuzla was established on a broad territory as a regional organisation sometime in June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And tell me, please, after this regional organisation which you've just mentioned, was a Croatian Community established in the Tuzla area and when, approximately?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know that for certain. At the head of this regional political organisation of the HVO was Mr. Pero Vasilj, whom I knew personally, and later on, sometime around September, I think, on the territory of the municipalities of Tuzla, Zivinice, Banovici, and Lukavac a Croatian Community called Soli was established headed by Mr. Zeljko Pestic who was its president. This Croatian Community of Soli joined the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna soon afterwards, sometime in October or November 1992, to the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, I'm very much interested in the creation of the Croatian Community of Soli who -- which, according to you, joined the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. And to your knowledge, those people getting together, what were their motives? Was that because they were given an order to get together, or was it because they felt themselves that given the situation, they had to get together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can tell you that I knew personally most of the people who established this Croatian Defence Council, as it first was called, and then the Soli community. They were not following somebody's orders. It was because of their assessment of the situation and its further development that they felt they should get together in order to protect the interests of the people living in the area, not just Croats but also Muslims and others, because I know for certain that when the HVO was established, representatives of other parties participated in that, not just of the HDZ, and also people who were not members of any party.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, can you tell me, please -- well, you've just told us about the establishment of the Croatian Community of Soli. Do you know what happened to the regional HVO community which, as you said, was established in June 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: With the establishment of the Croatian Community of Soli, this regional organisation of the HVO was abolished. And as I said, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna included Soli, Bosanska Posavina, Usora, Central Bosnia. All of these joined up into a common organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, you've already answered Judge Antonetti's question and my question about how the HVO units were established. Can you now explain to the Court, according to your information, when did these -- or, rather, when were these HVO units established on the territory of what was later call the 2nd Corps in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know that for certain, because I was there in the area. I know that smaller units of the HVO were established in the first half of 1992. I know that sometime in March 1992, for instance, a unit was established in Zivinice called the Zivinicki Sokolovi. I know that in the village of Drinica a friend of mine, Zvonko Juric, established a unit called Propatrija. I know that near Lukavac there was a small village called Bistravac [phoen], where a small HVO unit was formed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When mentioning Mr. Zvonko Juric, you mentioned the village Dremca [as interpreted] which has not enter the record.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Correction, Drinica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, that can be corrected later on. Mr. Makar, let us look at some documents illustrating what we've just been talking about. Please look at my binder. I see that the usher has given it to you. The first document is 1D -- I think it's an exhibit. 1925. Please take a look at the binder and tell me when you've found the document.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, document 1D1925 confirms what I said about the establishment of the regional community of the HVO on the territory of south-east Bosnia. You can see the date on page 4, which shows that this happened on the 12th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, one can see for this document that on the 12th of June, 1992, several representatives of political parties and of citizens established the Croatian Defence Council as a political organisation, and the goals are listed. Do you remember the name of the president of this first Croatian Defence Council established in June 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've already mentioned that I remember this very well. Unfortunately, he has died. His name was Pero Vasilj.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This document is already an exhibit. We have seen it before. Please look at the second document in my binder, 2D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document, as far as I can see, but if I'm mistaken please do not hesitate to correct me, but as far as I can see the political parties which set up the HVO originally in this region, you have the HDZ, the SDA, and then you also have the MBO, and it seems that there were other political parties as well, but there are two Muslim components, the SDA and the MBO. Are you in agreement that these political parties created the HVO in this region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you are right. Those were the three parties, but they were also representatives of the citizens, the people living in the area. I know that the MBO means the Muslim Bosniak Organisation. That was the name of the party. And I knew Mr. Salih Burek. He was a professor. Personally he was at the head of the party, and I think he participated in this. The Party of Democratic Action, the SDA, Professor Dr. Salih Kulenovic was their representative. I know him personally as well, and I believe that he also participated in this. So yes, I can confirm that what you have just said is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. You spoke about the fact that the Croatian Community was called Soli, and as we have a general testifying here, I didn't want to go too deeply into political issues. Just for the sake of the transcript, I want to say that the conclusion on the establishment of the community of Soli is already an exhibit, and its number is 1D2260, 1D2260, and I will be asking the witness about things he has direct knowledge of.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So please look at 1D1262 now. 2D. Not 1D but 2D1262. Just a moment, Mr. Makar, please. I'll put questions to you, and I think we'll proceed faster that way. Mr. Makar, these are minutes from the 5th session of the Presidency of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna held on the 17th of October in Travnik. On the last page of this document are the signatures of the attendees, and it says that this happened on the 17th of October, 1992. As we don't have the year on the first page, that's why I'm pointing this out. And here we have a list of those who attended the session. Please look at number 37. We see that there were some persons from Tuzla present. That's on page 2 of the document. And now we have the last page on e-court, but let's go back to page 2, please. So here we have a list of names, the names from Tuzla under number 37. Do you know the persons who attended this session of the Presidency of the HZ HB?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know Mr. Bozo Vilusic really well. I visited his father at his home about a month ago. As for Mr. Zeljko Pestic, I did know him but I haven't met him for a long time now. I think I also knew Mr. Ivica Antic, but I'm not sure about him.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now look at point 18 of the agenda, item 18, which is considering decisions -- the decision on the joining of the communities of Bosanska Posavina, Usora, and Central Bosnia. And let's look at this discussion under point 18 which is on page 15 in the Croatian version and 17 in English. Mr. Makar, so item 18, considering decisions on joining, and we have three communities, Bosnian Posavina, Central Bosnia, and Usora.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me. Ms. Nozica, unfortunately at least my copy of the English version does not have pagination, so maybe you could -- could tell us the -- the number that figures on the bottom right of the document. 0040 something or 50 something.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2D, as I see in e-court, 79-0056. I apologise to Their Honours. My copy does have pagination, but this document was translated again because there was something that had to be corrected. So now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I have the page. Thank you very much. No problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you. [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vilusic says here he informs those present that in north-east Bosnia in Tuzla, an HVO was established, the Croatian Community of Soli, and for objective reasons they have not been able to deliver their application to join. So now they want to join the unified HZ HB, a single HZ HB, and he goes on to report that within the scope of this community are municipalities, Banovici, Lukavac, and Zivinice. Would you please look at the end. This is on the next page, both in Croatian and in English, and it says here proposal to join the following Croatian communities to the unified community, Bosnian Posavina, Usora, Central Bosnia, the Soli community, and Sarajevo, and this has been adopted unanimously. The Soli community, just to have it correct in the transcript, it says the Soli community, S-o-l-i. Very well. We'll correct this later on. Mr. Makar, could you please identify whether this Soli community is the one that you mentioned, the one from Tuzla, and whether you have any knowledge that this is how things developed in September 1992 -- or in October 1992.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can confirm this because I spoke about this. Here we have the precise date when the Soli community from Tuzla joined the community of all the Croatian communities of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Makar. We'll now go back to military issues. Mr. Makar, under whose command were the HVO units acting on the territory of the 2nd Corps of the BH Army in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the HVO units acted under the command of the 2nd Corps, and let me clarify, these units were in the chain of command in all operative and combat issues and combat activities. As regards logistics, organisation, and the establishment of those units, the appointment of officers to those units, they were under the command of the Main Staff of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, would you now look at the following document, P10887.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. I'm still on document number 2D -- D1262. Witness, when I look at the list of the people who took part in the meeting of the 17th of October, 1992, I see Mr. Bozo Rajic, who is the vice-president or vice-chairman of the HZ HB, and deputy of head of defence. I have a question. Who was the head of defence? I'm going to explain this. Mr. Rajic, who was the deputy head because he's vice-president, or because he would be head of the Department of Defence or deputy of the Department of Defence or something like that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge Mindua, I can see this document, and I can see what you're referring to, but I can't explain it really because I didn't know of these relationships at the time. All I know is that later on Mr. Bozo Rajic was the minister of defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina. He occupied that post. That is what I do know, and that is what I can confirm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Perhaps I can clarify this. This is a document that you commented on. It is a meeting of the Presidency of the HZ HB. The witness just testified about people from Tuzla whom he knew, and at that time the witness was in the command of the 2nd Corps of the BH army in Tuzla, and he says that the rest of that structure is something that is not known to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, I asked for P10887, which is the next document. It is in fact a map, and I hope you've found it. A map of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it shows the separation lines dating to July 1993. And I've selected this map, Mr. Makar, because we showed it to the previous witness who was asked to indicate certain areas and some places were mentioned which came under the 2 be corps. So I'd like to ask the usher now to place this map on the ELMO this time so that the witness can mark the map. But just briefly, Mr. Makar. Just tell us -- you'll have to turn to the ELMO, the overhead projector, and please mark what the 2nd Corps incorporated, and please bear in mind that we're talking about 1992, from September onwards, up until the end of 1993 and beginning of 1994. So could you mark that on the map, all the areas incorporated by the 2nd Corps. It needn't be very precise, but just to give us an idea in the courtroom of how things stood geographically.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: I have a question, Your Honours. Am I being asked to state the places as municipalities, or just the borders?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, I asked you the question, actually, so just mark in the places.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: In the area of defence of the 2nd Corps we had the following places: Part of the Brcko municipality and Gradacac municipality, Gracanica; Doboj Municipality, part of it; Srebrenik, the whole of it; part of Lopare municipality; part of the Zvornik municipality; most of the Kalesija municipality and --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: While you're saying this, could you place an X on the map by each of those places that you've mentioned.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: All right I'll start again then. Brcko, Gradacac, Srebrenik, Gracanica, Doboj, Lopare, Zvornik, Vukovac, Zvinesik [phoen], Kalesija, Kladanj, Olovo, part of the Zavidovici municipality, Tesanj, and Maglaj, and part of the Zepce municipality. I think that's the lot.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. I was looking to see if you had incorporated Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you just initial the document so that we know that these markings were made by you.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Your Honours, although this document has a P number, because we have this witness's markings may it be given a C number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to give it an IC number. I think it's easier.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The document just marked by the witness shall be given Exhibit IC960. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In order for us to try and understand because everything is rather complex and difficult to grasp, as far as you're concerned, you are of Croat origin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I was born in Varazdin, a town in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand correctly, a Croat like you, you were part of the Main Staff of the 2nd Corps of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, you understood that correctly. I was the Chief of Staff and later on the deputy commander of the 2nd Corps of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, you were not the only person in that case. There were other Croats in the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Antonetti, you're quite right. In the 2nd Corps -- the first command of the 2nd Corps of the BH Army was my friend Mr. Zeljko Knez, who was also born in Croatia. The assistant for security issues was Mr. Anto Pranjic. He was also a Croat. He was born in Tuzla. The assistant for moral guidance was Mr. Dragan Kovacevic. The commander of the 107th HVO Brigade was Mr. Mijacevic. And in the Main Staff, as well of the Republic of BH Army, one of the three members of the top command was Mr. Stjepan Siber, born in Gradacac. And if need be, I can tell you other Croats who occupied top posts in the units of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. What you have said is on the transcript. That is precious information to understand everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, I'd like to ask you now, and we're still dealing with the units as we've just seen the 2nd Corps or territorially speaking what it looked like. 2D1154 now, please, which is the next document so that we can see what brigades came within the 2nd Corps. Mr. Makar, we see the date here, 1994, but before that, before that date, can you explain to the Trial Chamber what all the Xs mean above the rectangle -- rectangle number 2 where it says "Tuzla"? What is this schematic in fact? What does it show?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, these markings are the standard way in which the units were marked. The four stars were units of the rank of a corps. The number on the left-hand side was the number of the corps, and in this particular case the 2nd Corps, and the name underneath, Tuzla, was the 2nd Corps, Tuzla, the 2nd Tuzla Corps. Three stars or Xs above the OG 1 rectangles and the others were the divisions according to NATO standards. All this is according to NATO standards.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Makar, this was the situation in 1994, right, as far as the units under the 2nd Corps of the Bosnia-Herzegovina army in Tuzla are concerned. Can you explain to the Trial Chamber what units there were in 1992 and 1993 until the signing of the Washington Agreement? Was the situation somewhat different?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the situation in 1992 and 1993 was indeed somewhat different. At the time, the 2nd Corps had within it Operative Group 7, and I've already spoken about that. And within the composition of Operative Group 7, you had four brigades of the BH Army and the 110th Brigade of the Croatian Defence Council. Then in OG 1, Operative Group 1, there was just one brigade of the HVO and that was the 108th. And in OG 5, there was no 251st Brigade of the BH Army. So in conclusion, let me say that with the additions I've just presented, or amendments, this organisation of the 2nd Corps existed throughout, from 1992 right up until 1994, which is the schematic shown here with the exceptions I've just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, I'm curious about this. How is it that in an organisation chart we have Operation Group 7? It is not mentioned on this document. Why is that the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Antonetti, I'll explain that to you. Operative Group 7, for most of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, was physically cut off from the rest of the territory covered by the 2nd Corps. It was difficult to command those units. Now, with the reorganisation of the BH Army, which took place sometime in 1993, at the end of 1993, pursuant to an order from the Supreme Command of the BH Army, this Operative Group stepped outside the 2nd Corps composition; that is to say, from -- for exclusive operative and military reasons. It was no longer within the 2nd Corps composition.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, since at the very beginning of your testimony you said that in OG 1 -- that OG 1 included the 107th Brigade Gradacac, can we correct that too in the situation in 1994 -- or, rather, in 1992 and 1993 was that brigade under Operative Group 1, as you've already said?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I have already said that. That brigade did come under the Operative Group 1 in 1992 and 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. I now have some questions as follow-ups to Judge Antonetti's composition [as interpreted] with respect to the ethnic composition of the BH Army, and what I'm interested in is this: Can you tell us something about the national or ethnic composition of the HVO brigades which were within the composition of the 2nd Corps? What was the ethnic make-up in the HVO brigades?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes, I can give you a precise answer to that question because it's something I know about very well. The ethnic composition of almost all the units of the 2nd Corps was mixed. There was a mixed composition. There were Muslims and Croats and even some Serbs and others. The individual units of the 2nd Corps as the 2nd Tuzla Brigade, for instance, they had an ethnic composition which was almost identical to the ethnic composition of the population census of 1991. The 108th brigade of the HVO, which we've already mentioned, was a characteristic example because it had a mixed ethnic composition for the commander, the deputy, and three battalions with predominantly Muslim population or, rather, members, soldiers, and three battalions with predominantly Croatian soldiers, and the situation was similar in the 107th HVO Brigade except that there was the reverse ratio; that the commander, Mijacevic, was a Croat, the deputy was Sadam Imamovic, who was a Muslim, and the members of the brigade were mixed, of mixed composition. Now, as to the composition of the corps command, I've already spoken about that. That was also mixed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar can we just take a look at two documents to bear out what you said about the ethnic composition of the HVO brigades and units. Look at 2D1152 now, please, and just briefly explain to Their Honours what that is about?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a document in which I see the signature of Mr. Tomo Tokic, whom I knew personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. For the transcript, Mr. Makar. It was not recorded, the number was 2D1152. You can carry on now. I apologise for interrupting you.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document is signed by Tomo Tokic whom I knew personally, and I can also see that the document dates to July 1992, and I can also see that it is a list of individuals recorded for reinforcement of HVO units from Tuzla which was established and deployed to act in cooperation with the district Territorial Defence headquarters of Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, not to dwell too long on this document, you've looked through it, so I'd just like to ask you to confirm to the Trial Chamber, if you can, that the names with circles around them or the numbers with circles around them, that they are Muslim and Bosniak names. Just the names. We're not going to Muslim or Bosniak but Muslim or Bosniak names. Do you agree there? Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes, I can confirm that quite definitely because I know how many members -- how many Muslims were killed from the 115th Brigade, and some of them are on this list as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You can look at the next document, please, 2D1153, and just explain to us there again what the document is in relation to the first document we saw.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think that this document is a continuation of the previous document looking at the numbers of the people there listed and looking at the signature, which is once again that of Mr. Tomo Tokic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. You spoke, Mr. Makar, about the manner in which HVO units maintained contacts with the Main Staff, as you said, and you said that appointments and personnel affairs were dealt with in Mostar. So I'll ask you the following: Do you know in general how appointments were made in the HVO units which were part of the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know for certain that appointments of persons to particular positions in the brigades of the HVO which were part of the 2nd Corps were made by the Main Staff of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. So let's take a look at this. Look at 2D1530. That's the first document. 2D1530. This is not the document in e-court but you have found it, sir.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a decision relieving someone of their duty, and it's signed by Mr. Bruno Stojic as the head of the Defence Department. Can you confirm whether you know the persons who were relieved of their duty by this document? Do you know them, and does this document testify to what you've just said, that appointments, dismissals, and relieving people of their duty was -- were all done in Mostar, the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes, I can confirm this. I know these people. Mr. Zeljko Grgic is someone I know personally, and I still meet him frequently. I also know Mr. Pero Lovric. I might know the others, too, but I know for certain that I know these two.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, let's look at the following document, 2D1531. This is an appointment made to the 115th Brigade, Zrinjski, in Tuzla, and it's signed in 1993 by Mr. Stojic, and we see here that he is appointing nine persons, and it says at the end that other officers and employees in the brigade are to be appointed according to need by the brigade commander who is duty-bound to report this to the Defence Department of the HVO of the HZ HB. So first of all, I'll ask you did you know the persons appointed to these posts, numbers 1 to 9? Do you know some of them?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I know Mr. Marko Mijatovic, Mr. Mijo Cajic, Mr. Mijo -- sorry, Mr. Slavko Pecirep, and Mr. Josip Velfing. I know them personally, and as for Mr. Mijatovic and Mr. Cajic, together with commander of the 2nd Corps, I was at the celebration of the anniversary of the 2nd Brigade last year.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, from the last part of your reply, can we confirm that those people actually carried out the duties to which they were appointed by this document?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that these persons did carry out these duties.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It says here on page 2 that the commander of the 115th Zrinjski Brigade was authorised. Who was the commander at the time?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: The brigade of the 115th Zrinjski Brigade from the beginning to the end of the war was Mr. Zvonko Juric.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, do you know what the other contacts were like between the HVO brigades which were subordinated to the 2nd Corps and the Main Staff? Do you know of any other forms of contact or other forms of cooperation between the Main Staff, the Defence Department, and the HVO brigades which were subordinated to the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have already pointed out that the HVO brigades were subordinated to the command of the 2nd Corps in operative and combat activities, but as regards other military issues such as logistics, appointments, and other similar issues, they were subordinated to the Main Staff so that the HVO brigades and their commanders and other commanding officers regularly communicated with the Main Staff and the Defence Department in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, based on this document which concern the 115th Brigade of the HVO unless I'm mistaken this brigade is part of Operative Group 5. That's right. I've just checked. When Mr. Stojic, on the basis of this document, dismisses Mr. Marko Pavicic and relieves him of his duties, when he does this, I assume that a report was drafted by the authority of the 115th Brigade of the ABiH. That was addressed to Mr. Stojic to dismiss Mr. Marko Pavicic. It's not Mr. Stojic who meddles in the internal workings of the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is correct. The Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina had a similar principle. The Defence Departments dismissed and appointed officers of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in units and brigades of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. However, they did not interfere in any way, command other duties of these brigades, in this case the the 2nd Corps, so that Mr. Bruno Stojic as head of the Defence Department did this for the brigades of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. As far as you know Mr. Stojic was the head of the Defence Department, and as such did not have the authority to say no. If the ABiH asked him to dismiss Mr. Mirko Simic, head of the finance department, he dismissed him, or could he say that he did not agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can say that appointing and dismissing people to various posts in the units of the HVO was exclusively within the purview of the Defence Department of the HVO. The 2nd Corps never complained about any of the appointments or dismissals made in that way, but we were informed of all of them and we knew what appointments and dismissals had been made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall fine tune my question. Let's take the case of Mr. Mirko Simic. I don't know who this person is. It's number 4 on the list. I know that he was in charge of the budget and all financial matters relating to the brigade. When Mr. Stojic dismisses him, he dismisses him because it's the ABiH that has asked him to do so. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, no. That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why does he dismiss him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know why. The chief of the financial service in one of the brigades in the corps was relieved of his duty, although I was the Chief of Staff in that corps, but there were 35 brigades there. So with all due respect to Mr. Mirko Simic, that is a low-level officer. The level is too low for me to know the reasons why. We did not interfere in the appointments and dismissals of those persons who were considerably lower down in the military organisation. In the 2nd Corps command, we did not even interfere in some appointments at the rank of chief of the financial service in one of my brigades, for example, because this was not within the purview of the corps commander. He appointed officers at brigade level and the brigade commander had his own powers as did the Defence Department, and I think the same principle applied in the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, I don't know if I'm not mistaken when I say that, by answering this way you support the idea that between the HVO and the ABiH things were so inter-related that the Defence Department was, ex officio, in the position to appoint or dismiss officers even if these were lower-ranking officers without the ABiH intervening in any way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, precisely so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand correctly, let's assume that Mr. Stojic had wanted to dismiss you for whatever reason, could he have done so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't think I understood your question really well, but certainly Mr. Stojic could not have done that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I and officers at my level, at my rank, were appointed by the Defence Department and the Main Staff of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, as far as the higher-ranking officers at your level were concerned, Mr. Stojic couldn't do anything at all, but as far as lower-ranking officers were concerned, he could dismiss and appoint the former.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know what precisely were the powers of the Defence Department of the HVO and Mr. Stojic and up to what level and what officers he could dismiss and appoint, because that was not something I dealt with or was interested in at the time. In the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, there were precise rules as to what the Main Staff could do, what level of officers they could appoint and dismiss, and what the brigade commanders and lower-ranking officers could do. I think it was the same in the HVO. And this has to do with --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: He could dismiss and appoint the latter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, the witness did not finish his answer. He was interrupted. He did not finish the sentence, "and this has to do with," and then you interrupted. Please, please do not do this if possible. Let him finish the sentence. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I saw Judge Antonetti pointing at Mr. Praljak, and I intervened because I wanted to put my question before that because I think there is confusion arising from the question put by Judge Antonetti. At page 32, in line 17, His Honour Judge Antonetti asked about appointments in the 115th Brigade of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Witness, please, can you say once again very concisely, when it comes to appointments made by the Defence Department in Mostar, what units did these appointments relate to? Was it only the HVO units which were part of the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, His Honour Judge Trechsel just pointed out that I was interrupted in the middle of my sentence. Appointments and dismissals, the ones mention here and in general, in the brigades and units of the HVO, were exclusively within the competence of Mostar; whereas, appointments and dismissals in the units and brigades of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina were exclusively within the competence of Sarajevo, that is, the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Witness, I apologise to you. We have circled around this a lot. I think had this been stated earlier, there would have been less confusion. I don't know whether Mr. Praljak wanted to say anything else?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you want to clarify something because I do not quite understand answer from the witness, but perhaps you can give us some clarification. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honours, witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But not clarify as a witness. You're just going to clarify the situation. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] I don't want to testify, Your Honour. I'm always being told this. I don't see that I'm testifying. But please ask him. It's very important for you to clarify what is operative and combat subordination or resubordination of one army to another or units from one army to other units, and what is retaining logistics, staffing policy, personnel, and so on. And is that how it works in all the forces of NATO and so on? So this is something that has to be ultimately clarified. Resubordination in combat and operations while retaining the autonomy of the army coming from France or any other country which is part of an alliance, because that is the essence of the proposals discussed later on the 15th of January and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you for this clarification. In the question that I asked earlier on, this was this issue that I wanted to bring about when I was talking about the interrelation between both armies. General Praljak talked about the resubordination of an army and -- towards another, and you haven't really touched upon this issue, hence my question earlier on. Would it be correct to say that in February 1993, the 115th brigade of the HVO had been subordinated to the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Antonetti, Mr. Praljak said precisely the same thing that I said, but perhaps you didn't note that properly. It's in the transcript, and I said quite literally what he just said, that the brigades of the Croatian Defence Council were resubordinated to the 2nd Corps of the BH Army Corps in the operative and combat sphere, and as the Chief of Staff, or, rather, the corps commander, I was not interested in who was the head of the financial service in that brigade if it was in operative and combat terms working properly under our command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. I wonder whether I understand this or correct -- I think I -- mainly, I do understand it, but perhaps you do not know the structure of the competencies within the HVO and Mostar. The Defence Department was competent as far as the chiefs of services in the staff were concerned, medical service, security, and so forth, because they formed part of the Ministry of Defence. Was he also competent with regard to commanders within the HVO Brigade? Do you know that or is that something that you did not bother about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge Trechsel, I don't know that much about that topic, and you've said it precisely. I don't know the relationships between the Main Staff of the HVO and the Defence Department that well. I think they were responsible for appointing brigade commanders of the HVO as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we have to take a break, but the question from my colleague was at a different level than my question which had to do with the subordination. The main issue was to find out whether the HVO brigades had been resubordinated to the ABiH. This is this is really what is at hand here, this issue of resubordination, I would like to know whether there was a document coming from the Main Staff of the ABiH or of the HVO, to your knowledge of course, a document stating that the 115th brigade was a part, whether forever or just for a period of time, of this 2nd Corps. Was there a document and, if so, have you seen this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know whether any such document existed, because from the beginning of 1992, I was the assistant for operations and training, and later on the Chief of Staff of the corps, and so my prime task was to deal with combat operations, and that is why I was in the field engaged in combat operations. These other questions were in the administrative domain and had to do with personnel, cadres. The corps commander dealt with those matters together with his assistants for personnel affairs and organisational affairs. So I can't confirm that because I don't know if any such document existed. And for my part, what was essential as far as I was concerned was that those brigades carry out their combat orders that they received from the command of the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So according to you, you were working on the ground. You had the 115th Brigade at your disposal. Now, whether this 115th brigade had been subordinated or how it had been subordinated or how the department of the defence of the HVO was working with the Main Staff of the HVO this -- this was not part of your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since I'm not sure, I wouldn't like to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. We're going have a break of 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall resume. Just a point of clarification for tomorrow's hearing. Since we have a Plenary Session which will start at 2.30 -- at 12.30, will start at 12.30 and finish at 1430 or 1400, in order for us to be prepared, we will start this hearing at 14.30, 2.30 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, now we have to clarify at least three points. Now, for the transcript I'd like to say that on page 22 of today's testimony and today's transcript, lines 2 to 7, you said in answer to my question that all the HVO brigades which were within the composition of the 2nd Corps acted under the command of the 2nd Corps in a combat and operative terms, and in the logistics sense, organisational and administrative sense, they were under the responsibility or authority as you said of the Main Staff. Now, because of the series of questions that you were asked by the Judges, could you once again confirm whether you stand wholly by what you said earlier on in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes, I do stand wholly by what I said earlier on and what Ms. Nozica has just repeated and summarised.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Judge Antonetti afterwards asked you whether there was a document about this to the effect that the HVO brigades which were within the composition of the 2nd Corps in combat terms, whether they were subordinated to the 2nd Corps of the BH Army, and you said that you didn't know whether any such document or decree existed. Now, I'm asking you whether you as someone who was a high-ranking individual in the command of the 2nd Corps of the BH Army, whether you know that the 2nd Corps -- or, rather, the BH Army commanded those units?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I certainly do know that the 2nd Corps did command those units. And let me repeat, in combat operations they carried out the combat tasks and assignments just as the BH Army brigades did. Let me make that clear now by quoting an example. At a certain point in time, a smaller unit of the 115th Brigade of the HVO left part of the battle-field, and I as Chief of Staff at that point in time of the corps, I engaged the military police of the BH Army, and they arrested and took those soldiers into custody and having spent a night in prison, the next day they carried out their tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In line -- or, rather, page 41, line 8, it should read -- did you say that was November of what year? The 115th Brigade, you said, is that right, of the HVO, or the 115th Brigade of the BH Army, which? I'm referring to your last answer?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: They were members of the 115th Brigade of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. That's fine. We've cleared that up. And one more explanation linked to the appointments we've mentioned so far. We saw the appointments and how people were relieved of duty in the 115th HVO Brigade and that was in 2D1530. So we're going back and 2D1531; right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. That's precisely right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, can you confirm, please, Mr. Makar, that all the appointments and when people were relieved of their duties were pursuant to proposals from the command of this brigade?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that because that's what the practice was, and that was what the practice in the BH Army units was as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, we left off discussing command for the 2nd Corps and communications between the HVO of the brigades who were within the 2nd Corps. Did you have and do you have any knowledge and experience about the following: That certain parts of other brigades, other HVO brigades, from the HZ HB came onto the territory of the 2nd Corps as reinforcement either to the 2nd Corps of the HVO brigades which belonged to the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes, I can confirm that. Smaller parts of the HVO units from the broader area around Mostar and the Main Staff, did come to the area of defence of the 2nd Corps of the BH Army as reinforcement in the very difficult combat operations, and if there's enough time, I can also quote some examples where I took part personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, if -- when these units arrived in the territory of the 2nd Corps, and you say you have examples where you took part personally, can you tell us who commanded them? Who was in command in the area of responsibility of the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: They were smaller units of a platoon level, and to explain to Their Honours that means about 30 men, 30 soldiers. And when arrived in the area of responsibility of the 2nd Corps, defence of the 2nd Corps, they were subordinated to the brigade in whose area they were active, and by that same token they were under 2nd Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you personally command those units? Have you got any personal experience?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. I can say unfortunately I do have personal experience in that. It was sometime at the end of 1992 when I was up at the front line of the fighting that was taking place in the area of Markovic Polje and Laniste. It was in the area of our 107th Brigade, and as reinforcement from the Mostar area, a smaller unit numbering about 30 men arrived. They were well-trained soldiers, and right next to me during the fighting some were seriously wounded. And I can quote another example which I happen to remember just now, where in the area of defence of the 108th Brigade and the 21st Brigade of the BH Army, Mr. Ante Roso and Mr. Niko Lozancic brought in a platoon of specials of the HVO into the area of Islamovac near Brcko where there was heavy fighting going on, and I went up to the front line with them, into the front line, and unfortunately next to me two of those soldiers were killed by my side.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now that you've mentioned the 108th Brigade, it was the HVO 108th Brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, with respect to communication and the communication lines, the HVO, the brigade, Main Staff, and Defence Department, let's look at 2D00439, the next document, please. We have a request here from Mr. Bruno Stojic dated the 20th of May, 1993, requesting complete information on the situation in Tuzla and Brcko. And I'd like us to move to the second document now, please, or, rather, the second page of this document where we have a response dated the 21st of May, 1993, signed by the commander. It is the 115th Zrinjski HVO Brigade which was within the composition of the 2nd Corps of the BH Army, and it is signed by Zvonko Juric. Can you first confirm for Their Honours that Mr. Juric was indeed the commander of this brigade? Do you know that personally?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Mr. Zvonko Juric was the commander of the 115th Brigade of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, would you explain to the Trial Chamber -- well, we have a report -- or, rather, a piece of information dated the 21st of May, 1993. Can you explain to the Trial Chamber the circumstances in which this document was compiled and whether you, yourself, were in Mostar beforehand and provided information about the events taking place at that time to the representatives of the Defence Department?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can give you an explanation. Looking at this document, it was probably compiled during the very heavy fighting that was going on the battlefront in Posavina, north of Tuzla. Before that, sometime at the end of April and the beginning of May, I happened to be in Mostar, and I informed Mr. Stojic, Petkovic, and Praljak of the very difficult situation that we were facing over there in our area. Now, I didn't know about this document at the time, the one we're looking at just now, but looking at it now I assume that after my visit to Mostar and after having informed them of the very difficult situation, Mr. Stojic must have asked the commander of the 115th HVO Brigade to inform him personally about the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Makar, in the middle of that document, just above point 3, it says: "However, there is a lack of MTS, materiel and technical equipment, as well as a full logistical support which can have strategic consequences and destabilise the entire battle-field." Were you aware of this situation at that time, and did you discuss it previously with the representatives, as you say, with Mr. Stojic, Petkovic, and Praljak?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the situation with respect to MTS and the lack of it was chronic, if I can use that term. Throughout the war, there was always a lack of MTS, a shortage, and the opposite side has had endless resources which we always lacked. So I was at the end of April and beginning of May in Mostar precisely for that reason, to try and secure replenishment with MTS.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, in point 5 it says in this document that the political and security situation in the Tuzla region was stable, that there were no conflicts with the BH Army, and that the 2nd Corps command completely honoured the agreement reached in Zagreb on the 25th of April, 1993, and pertains to the articles dealing with (A), that the BH Army and the HVO will keep their own separate identities and command constitutions, and the ARBiH are equally legal armies, and that the ABiH and HVO have joint command for the district of -- that the Joint Command for the district of Tuzla is still not established because General Halilovic did not appoint two of his officers. So this agreement could not have been implemented. Can you confirm that that was the situation in Tuzla and that the information set out here is correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that, and that throughout the war the situation in Tuzla and further afield in the territory covered by the 2nd Corps was as has been described and that what Mr. Zvonko Juric says here is quite correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. As you have just touched on the main topic of your testimony, which is procurement of equipment and materiel, can you explain to Their Honours how in terms of logistics the 2nd Corps was supplied with equipment and materiel, both the corps as a whole and the HVO units which were a part of it.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the 2nd Corps, in order to engage in combat activities, procured equipment and materiel in several ways. One way was through the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia, directly from Croatia. The other way was through the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia and through the Grude logistics base. The third way was from the logistics base of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Visoko. The fourth way was directly from the supplies of the HVO in the Grude logistics base. The fifth way was through logistics centres of the BH Army in Zagreb, and the logistics centres of individual brigades and municipalities in Zagreb. And the last way was by direct donations of certain equipment and materiel for the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: As you've mentioned various sources of supplies of equipment and materiel for the 2nd Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, can you tell us from which source you received the most equipment and materiel?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: We received most of the equipment and materiel for the 2nd Corps from the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia and the Grude logistics base.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
