utterances.text: Please explain to Their Honours how the first contacts were established and with whom regarding procurement of material and equipment, either with the HVO or the logistics base in Grude. Who established these contacts?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the first contacts were established by the commander of the 2nd corps, Zeljko Knez, and then these contacts were continued by Hazim Sadic, General Hazim Sadic, who was later the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You spoke about the first commander of the 2nd corps, Mr. Zeljko Knez. Until when was he the commander of the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Mr. Zeljko Knez was the commander of the 2nd Corps until February 1993. He then received an order from the Supreme Command Staff of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina appointing him military attache of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the embassy to the Republic of Croatia, but as far as I know, this order was never implemented in practice.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So as far as you know, he never became the military attache of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Croatia. Does that mean that in February he left the duty of the commander of the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. He never became a military attache but he left in February.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you just tell us who was appointed in his place?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Hazim Sadic was appointed in place of Zeljko Knez. Up to that point in time, he had been deputy corps commander and he became acting corps commander at that point. He was acting commander until the 18th of July, 1993, when he was officially appointed corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, you mentioned Mr. Sadic and Mr. Knez regarding supplies of materiel and equipment. In 1992, were there any contacts with the Ministry of Defence in Croatia in order to obtain medical equipment and materiel?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. We had quite a few war hospitals which needed medicines and other supplies, so Mr. Hazim Sadic, sometime in August 1992, established direct contact with Mr. Ivo Prodan, who was a physician and a head doctor, and he was in the health administration of the Ministry of Defence of Croatia, and based on his contacts with Mr. Sadic, we received the medical equipment and supplies we needed for our war hospitals and other needs.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you now look at 2D1038, please. It's the next document. It's an order. We have it in e-court now. Could you please very briefly say whether this is a command that has to do with these contacts you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think this is the order stating that Mr. Sadic was to carry out this task and to be allowed to move about freely while performing it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, after these contacts established by Mr. Knez and Mr. Sadic, did contacts continue, and was other equipment and materiel obtained apart from medical supplies for the 2nd Corps, weapons and so on?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. These contacts continued. We received large amounts of medical material for our war hospitals because we had large numbers of casualties in our combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, as you spoke of different ways of procuring materiel and equipment, you said one of these ways was directly from the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia. So I would now like to ask you to look at a few documents and comment very briefly and then we'll deal with all of them together as a set. So please look at 2D1046, please.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a dispatch note for equipment and materiel, and you can see that this was sent from Zagreb through the Ministry of Defence for the 107th Brigade of the Gradacac HVO, and we see who the driver was who received these goods.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, as it says here that it's for the 107th Gradacac Brigade, can you explain to Their Honours whether this equipment was being sent to the 107th Brigade only and why is the 107th Brigade mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the 2nd Corps when entering its area had a check-point through which all equipment and material entering the corps area had to pass. Pursuant to an agreement with the HVO, all the equipment being sent to the 2nd Corps was addressed in the documents to the 107th Brigade of the HVO or the 108th Brigade or the 115th Brigade, and it was the corps that disposed of all the equipment and distributed them where it was most needed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This agreement which you say was in place at the time, did it refer to equipment and materiel arriving directly from Croatia as well?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this pertained to all the equipment and materiel arriving, and the reason it was done was so that this equipment could pass more easily through areas controlled by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, you yourself said that you went to Mostar to the main logistics base in order to obtain equipment and materiel. Did the 2nd Corps of the BH Army issue approval for safe passage when obtaining this MTS through areas controlled by the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, precisely so. The documents had to be addressed in this way, because there was a war going on, and there were many local commanders around who didn't always comply with orders coming from above. So in order to ensure safe passage, we from the 2nd Corps also issued our documents for the passage of this equipment and materiel through the territory held by the army of -- the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, let's look at the following four documents which also relate to what we are just discussing. 2D1093. Can you just confirm whether this was material for the 2nd Corps arriving from Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm that this was being sent from Zagreb to the 2nd Corps, and you can see that this was received by Mr. Edin Delibegovic. He was the assistant commander of the 2nd Corps for procurement.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well the next document 2D1150.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I confirm that this is a similar document with Mr. Edin Delibegovic taking a delivery on behalf of the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I also can confirm that this document deals with the supply of various types of equipment and materiel for the needs of the 2nd Corps, and it came from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And document 2D1040. It's dated the 16th of February, 1993, and signed by the chief of the department of the Ministry of the Interior, a service for the protection of the constitutional order. Can you very briefly comment on this document.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: We can see from this document that the chief of the department, Mr. Cedomir Dijanovic, is asking for approval for transport of equipment and materiel, asking that it be allowed to leave Split, and that the equipment be delivered to its destination in Tuzla and Gradacac. He goes on to mention that he will inform the commander of the 2nd Corps, Mr. Zeljko Knez, and the commander of the Gradacac battlefront, Mr. Miocevic in order for them to take delivery of the equipment and materiel.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Does this document confirm that the equipment arrived on the territory of the 2nd Corps as you explained?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And finally can we confirm how these weapons, when they arrived in the 2nd Corps, how they were distributed?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: The weapons which arrived in the 2nd Corps were recorded by the logistics services of the corps, and then distributed to the brigade or Operative Group which needed them most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Makar, with respect to the document 2D01040, you have confirmed that the document shows that these MTS were actually delivered. I read at the -- at the bottom of the letter as follows: "We are going to duly inform you on the time of the team's arrival as well as about individuals who are the members of the team." It does not seem to me that this shows that it was actually delivered. On the contrary, it announces the delivery and announces confirmation. Now, maybe I am in error and have misunderstood something, but perhaps you can explain. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you understood correctly. I didn't say that these particular supplies arrived. I was only saying that the document shows the procedure and the methods used when transporting this equipment. Approval was necessary, and after the approval was obtained, the 2nd Corps was informed. I can't say whether this particular equipment arrived, so, yes, you understood this correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The record does not actually render this the same way, if you look at 51, page 51, lines 11 to 13, but you have clarified now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have a question for you. I don't know if you'll be able to answer it. If you don't answer my question, I shall keep this document and put the question to other witnesses who will come here and who come from the Republic of Croatia in the event that someone can answer my question, but maybe you are able to answer my question. On looking at this document 2D1040, I realise something. This document stems undoubtedly from the Republic of Croatia and the Interior Ministry, but I see that it says here "Department for the protection of the constitutional system," and this raises a question. Was this department only designed to ensure the protection of the Republic of Croatia, or did -- or was this department competent to protect the constitutional system of other republics? Can you shed some light on this or don't you know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I really can't say what the system of organisation was and whether the service for the protection of the constitutional system, where it was, but as -- well, actually, I assume that it was there for the protection of the constitutional system of the Republic of Croatia, because it says the Republic of Croatia in the heading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, let's move on to another kind of procurement of materiel and equipment for the needs of the 2nd Corps. Can you explain to Their Honours whether the 2nd Corps in a certain period of time obtain MTS from Bosnia and Posavina and, to the best of your knowledge, how this was agreed and with whom? After that we'll look at some documents.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we obtained MTS from Bosanska Posavina, also from the depot of the HVO for as long as this was possible. Later on, when due to combat activities engaged in by the Chetnik forces, our connections with Bosnian Posavina were cut off. We could no longer obtain MTS from there, and then we could only obtain it from Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Would you now take a look at document 2D1075. Mr. Makar, once again let's see whether this refers to MTS for the 2nd Corps and its procurement, and can you just tell us whether what it says here about the 107th Brigade, that that was in fact pursuant to the agreement that you spoke about earlier on?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes, I can confirm that. This document, as we can see, is about MTS coming from Bosanska Posavina, and we can see that it is addressed to the 107th HVO Brigade. However, from a detail here which I've just noticed, what I said is confirmed, and that is that the materiel and resources were handed out by the 2nd Corps where they were most needed. And would you focus on number 4 for that, please, number 4, point 4 of this document, where it says round of bullet, 100 millimetres, T-12. And since I'm well-versed in these matters, a T-12 cannon is something that the 107th HVO Brigade never had. And as you can see, a hundred grenades arriving for that particular cannon, gun, which confirms that in one shipment of this MTS, materiel merchandise were intended for other units of the corps as I've already said.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I have quite a number of documents to get through, and you can just tell me whether you confirm that this was done in the same way and the next document is 2D1076.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm that that is correct. It's the same way, method.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now 2D1044.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: I can confirm that, too, that it was done in the way I've described.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: 2D1045 is the next document.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm that too.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: 2D1047 is next.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that. The principle is the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And 2D1068.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that for this document as well. The same principle was applied for the procurement of MTS.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, linked to these documents, can you confirm that these weapons did indeed reach Tuzla and were distributed in the way you've described to us?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes, I can confirm that, that the weapons and MTS did arrive at the 2nd Corps and that it was later used in the manner I have already described.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, do you know whether this MTS was issued out for the needs of the 2nd Corps in conformity with permission and knowledge of the Main Staff in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that, because when the MTS arrived to the brigades of the HVO, they used their own lines to send reports to the Main Staff of the HVO, and from that we were able to see which resources actually arrived.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, a moment ago you explained to us all the ways and channels in which the MTS reached the 2nd Corps, and you said that you procured them also from the logistics base at Grude, and you explained that this was done in two ways. Could you repeat how the MTS arrived in Grude and how you procured them?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Part of the MTS would arrive through the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia and Grude and was then sent on to the 2nd Corps, and part of the MTS, the other part of the MTS, came directly from the depots in Grude and arrived in the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. So that was a warehouse and depot under HVO control; right? That's quite clear.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. That was the main logistics base of the HVO of Grude, and that's quite clear. It was the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, since we're talking about the first way in which the resources were sent from MORH, and you took them over, or, rather, the 2nd Corps took them over in Grude, for that let's just look at four documents and I'll ask you for your comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have a follow-up question for you. In the last document which is dated -- dated the month of April, if I'm not mistaken, wasn't there an arms embargo at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Antonetti, I'm a professional soldiers, and in peacetime and wartime I adhered to the principle that politics determines and the army carries things out. So it's not my place to comment the questions of embargo. That's a political decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand your question. As inside the 2nd Corps, were there international observers? Were there any liaison officers part of the 2nd Corps who were in contact with you, with your colleagues, or with higher-ranking officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Antonetti, in the area of responsibility of the 2nd Corps, from the beginning of the war until the end of it, there were always international observers present. First of all it was UNPROFOR, the military forces, then observers from the European Community and then other organisations as well, and as the Chief of Staff, it was one of my duties every Tuesday, whenever I wasn't in the field, to hold meetings with those organisations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the international observers saw, for instance, that elements of the 107th Brigade had 20 RPG 7s that were brand new, did they tell you that they were a little bit surprised by that, or did that seem quite normal? In the document, 24 RPGs were supplied.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Antonetti, I'm in a difficult place here to answer the question, because we're dealing with members of the international forces, after all, who performed their duties honourably, the assignments they were given, and as to their conduct in the field, that very often depended on certain local conditions. But if you would like, I can give my own comments, and they would be this: After meeting them over a period of time and holding meetings with the representatives of the international community over a long period of time, when we came into closer contact and I got to know them better, they told me loud and clear -- they said, "General, sir, we are here first and foremost to implement the policies of our governments. Secondly, we are here because it's well paid. Thirdly, is our role to assist you." Well, I apologise for being frank, but that is an exact rendition of what I was told by them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Two questions after Judge Antonetti's questions. First of all, Judge Antonetti says if the observers were to see these 24 RPGs in the 107th HVO Brigade, I think it would be well to repeat once again. Those mortars, did they come to the 107th HVO Brigade, or did they arrive at the 2nd Corps and then were distributed according to need, which?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: All the MTS that arrived from any source whatsoever had to go through just one route. Physically, it was not possible to bring them in through any other route, so that it was the 2nd Corps which received all the MTS through that one route and kept complete records of their arrival. After that, let me repeat, we would distribute these resources to the parts of the front where they were most needed regardless of what brigade, whether it was the HVO Brigade or BH Army brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, another question. Following on from the questions asked by Judge Antonetti, what would have happened to the Tuzla region, which as we have seen is a very large area, had you not procured weapons in the way in which you have described to us now during your testimony? Would the area have been defended from the Yugoslav Army and Serb paramilitaries? Would it have been successful in defending itself?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, perhaps I wouldn't be sitting here today, because one thing is certain, the territory could not have been defended successfully without those weapons. And I can also say that in the NATO school that I attended after the war, we were there together with Serb officers, and we had mutual discussions and discussed matters like that, that they had a thousand shells during the war on one day and we had ten. Had we not even had those ten shells, then quite certainly the territory would look quite different today to what it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, you mentioned in response to my questions -- well, you said that the MTS came from the Ministry of Defence of Croatia to the logistics base in Grude, and then you took the MTS over from there. Have I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now look at document 2D1155 and tell us whether this is a document confirming this manner of procurement, 1155 is the document number.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours I've found the document and that is confirmation of what I've been talking about, because we can see that the MTS transport was okayed from Imotski-Grude-Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The next document is 2D1090. Is that a document confirming the fact that those resources went to the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. That is what it confirms, precisely, because there's an order saying that it should go through the central logistics base Grude, and we can see that it is from the Ministry of Defence of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, let's stay with this document for just a moment. It says here for the requirements of the 115th HVO Brigade Zrinjski, and it is signed by Edin -- or rather, it's taken over by Edin Delibegovic, the MTS was taken over by Edin Delibegovic, and here you said that he was a logistics man of the 2nd Corps; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: I'm not sure what document you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: 1090 is the one we're talking about, and it's just been called up on e-court. Do you have it on your screen.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: No mention is made of the 115th Brigade there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: 1090 on e-court. Perhaps you're looking at the wrong document. HVO, the 115th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: No, no mention is made of the 115th Brigade there. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It says for the HVO the 115th Brigade. Look at the next document then, please. It says 10 -- I do apologise. It's my mistake. 1091. Yes, my mistake. It's a mistake on the document. 1091; is that right? That it was going to the 115th Brigade and signed by the logistics operator?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Well, no mention is made of the 115th there, either.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: 1091 is the document number, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, you must be making a mistake. The witness is extremely precise. 115 isn't in there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes. The mistake is on the document that I have before me, but let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Look at 2D1091, please. Is that the same method of procurement?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The document does show this method.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Right. Now look at 1095 the next document, please.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: That's all right too. The same principle applied.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Makar, you stated that had when it came to the Grude logistics base, part of the MTS arrived from Croatia, and the other part you took over directly from the warehouse and depot at Grude. Now look at 2D1048, the next document, please. 2D1048.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we have your comments on the first document so that we can look at the rest?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. This is the principle I talked about, directly for the central logistics base in Grude from HVO resources from the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We have to go back a bit because it says the 107th Brigade Gradacac. Does that mean that regardless of that title that it all went for the requirements of the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's now look at 2D1050, the next document, please.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: I can confirm that the same way of procurement was applied. The warehouse was Gabela, but it came under the control of the central logistics base at Grude.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mention is made here of the 107th and 108th Brigade, and the date is rather important. It is the 26th of February, just like in the previous document. Well, the previous document was the 8th and now it's the 26th of February, 1993. Right, Mr. Makar?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The next document is 2D1049.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's the same method of procurement. We can see that from the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, the next document is 2D1070, and in this document the date is the 26th of March, 1993. What about those MTS? Do they come from Grude for the requirements of the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. We can see that the Main Staff gave permission for the MTS to be taken from Grude and that they were sent to the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now look at 2D1069 which contains two such dispatch notes.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I confirm that the same thing holds true there, and the date is the 27th of March. This is an example of the same principle, MTS for the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And the same applies to the 28th of March; right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now look at 2D1059. Here it says HVO Gradacac, 107th Brigade. Yes, correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. Correct. I can see in the heading where the equipment is coming from. It's the same method of procurement I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, let's look at 2D1043. This approval was signed by Mr. Praljak on the 20th of February, 1993. Can you see any familiar names here, and do you know whether this MTS really was sent for the needs of the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document again confirms that this is how HVO materiel was dispatched to the 2nd Corps. I know Mr. Esad Hanic. He was the logistics man in the 107th HVO Brigade in Gradacac.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And let's look at 2D1041, signed by Mr. Stojic, and it's addressed to Ismet Mehmedovic from Gradacac. In other words, he is given safe conduct, and can you tell us whether this was also materiel sent for the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. This approval again shows how MTS was dispatched from the HVO depot for the 2nd Corps. I don't know Mr. Ismet Mehmedovic personally. It says here that he was from Gradacac, and I believe he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, mention is made in these documents of Mr. Praljak and Mr. Stojic. Was there an agreement with these gentlemen about the procurement of MTS from the logistics base for the needs of the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've already spoken about this. This agreement did exist from the first contacts of Mr. Zeljko Knez, and later on until the end of the war this is how the agreement was implemented.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, you said that you personally participated in procurement of MTS. Please tell us briefly if you went to Mostar, how many times did you go and at what times, approximately? When?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I did go to Mostar in order to make sure that supplies of MTS were sent. First -- the first time I went was in February 1993 or thereabouts. Then I visited Mostar again in March, about a month later, and my third visit took place sometime in late April or early May 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, when you arrived in Mostar for the first time, as you say, in February 1993, who was with you? On whose orders did you go there, and who did you meet when you arrived in Mostar? With whom did you discuss the possibility of taking over delivery of MTS?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I was with two other officers from the 2nd Corps, Mr. Ivan Mijacevic from the 107th Brigade of the HVO, and Mr. Osman Puskar, the commander of Operative Group 2. My departure to Mostar was based on an order there commander, Hazim Sadic, and the purpose was to ensure the delivery of MTS.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, when you arrived in Mostar, how long did you stay there and with whom did you discuss procurement of MTS?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can't remember precisely how long we stayed, maybe two or three days. The team from the 2nd Corps which I mentioned had talks with representatives of the HVO in Mostar, Mr. Praljak, Mr. Stojic, Mr. Petkovic, Mr. Bozo Rajic. I think that's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We can now look at several documents confirming what you've just said. 2D1103.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I remember this authorisation authorising me to conduct talks and sign contracts regarding logistics on behalf of the 2nd Corps, and it was signed by the commander Hazim Sadic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The next document is 2D1105.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this sort of approval was always issued allowing us to use an all-terrain vehicle and a car to go to Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could we have 2D1102.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this was evidently issued while we were there on the 23rd of February after we had conducted talks. Mr. Bozo Rajic was the minister of defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Mostar, with its headquarters in Mostar, issued an order that I and the two officers who were with me be allowed safe passage and correct treatment, and that the person accompanying the MTS also be granted safe conduct. Based on our talks, we received certain quantities of MTS. I think these were two or three truckloads which we brought to the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you now look at 2D1111.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I didn't understand this document 1102. It says Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Ministry of Defence, Mostar. The Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina had an office in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the minister of defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Bozo Rajic, was then in Mostar. I don't know how this was regulated, but in my view it shows that the minister of defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was where the Defence Department was, the Defence Department of Herceg-Bosna, and this shows that this was not in dispute. There was nothing contentious there. If you allow me to go back, even now after the war certain ministries are dislocated and are relocated elsewhere outside Sarajevo. Certain sessions of the cabinet are also held outside the capital, but if a minister is in another location, he's still the minister of that state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm asking you this question because it's the first document of this type that I see, and this document seems to establish the fact that the government of Sarajevo had a post in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and you say that the Ministry of Defence was relocated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can't assert this, but that was my understanding while I was there, and I see the same in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But when you went to Mostar, did you pay a visit to Mr. Bozic Rajic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, absolutely. I mentioned that he attended all our talks. And after our talks I spoke to him separately. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And where was his office?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know precisely what office belonged to whom, but after talking in a room where we were all together, he invited me to a separate room, and I remember that on the door it said "Minister of Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Bozic Rajic." I even think he gave me his visiting card with that title. I think I might have kept it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in his office was there a flag from the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I really don't recall that, because at the time what mattered to me was to obtain MTS. So I didn't pay attention to these details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Ms. Nozica can continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, you say you were received by the minister of defence, Mr. Bozic Rajic. Please clarify to Their Honours the following: You had arrived from the 2nd Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you consider him to be the minister of defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's now look at document 2D1111, which also mentions Mr. Rajic. And please clarify to Their Honours very briefly what this document means. It was signed by Hazim Sadic. The date is the 20th of February, 1993, but we see when it was sent, and you will clarify what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, at these meetings in Mostar we talked with the persons I've already mentioned, not only about the procurement of MTS but also about certain issues which were of interest to both sides. I was authorised to engage in these talks on behalf of the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and on behalf of the commander of the 2nd Corps. This is evident from the preamble to this document where it says: "Pursuant to an order issued by the chief of the staff of the Supreme Command." The document was compiled on my return to the 2nd Corps in Tuzla. I personally composed the document, and you can see this if you look at page 2, in the lower left-hand corner you see the initials AM. Those are my initials through the A. The principle was for the compiler of the document to put his initials there, and the other set of initials belonged to the typist. The document was actually a report from the 2nd Corps sent to the staff of the Supreme Command, for the staff of the Supreme Command to be informed of what had been discussed and agreed at those meetings. The document was signed, of course, by the commander, because he signed every document. And please pay attention to page 2, the lower left-hand corner. It was sent to the president of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, to the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command, Mr. Sefer Halilovic, to the commander of the staff of the armed forces, Mr. Rasim Delic, and to the head of the HVO Herceg-Bosna, Mr. Bruno Stojic, which was quite normal and natural because we wanted to inform him of the way in which we had reported on our talks.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, if I understood you correctly, this reports are refers to more than one meeting. It's all the meetings and contacts you had in the course of your visit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You say here in item 1, 1(A): "Representatives of the HVO of Herceg-Bosna are fully prepared to consistently implement all the items of the agreement between the Presidency president, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic, and the president of the Republic of Croatia, Mr. Franjo Tudjman." And under (C): "Representatives of the HVO Herceg-Bosna are offering the formation of a Joint Command," and they have a proposal in this regard. But now I'd like to deal with logistics. Further on in this document it says logistics (A). Was this the main reason why you went to Mostar, to agree on procurement of MTS? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It says here under (A): "After becoming familiar with the situation in the 2nd Corps, where all of the ABiH and HVO units are under a Joint Command ..." His Honour Judge Antonetti asked whether there was a single document from which this is evident. Can we confirm that this is such a document? It was sent both to Mr. Alija Izetbegovic and to the Chief of Staff, Sefer Halilovic, and it clearly shows that you say here that all the units of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. West.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. My apologies for standing up and interrupting. There have been a number of times where counsel's questions have been leading, and I've not been commenting on them because I know she has a number of documents to go through, but this last question was I think a bit more than any of the others, and I would just like to point it out for the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, please be careful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. It was only leading because it was a follow-up question to His Honour's question, but I won't do that anymore.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So would you comment on this, Witness. Would you comment on this part of your report under 2(A)?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: I can confirm that this manner of distribution --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But that's not my question. I'm asking you about logistics (A), the first part of your sentence. "After becoming familiar with the situation in the 2nd Corps where all of the units of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the units of the HVO are under a Joint Command." Mr. Makar, did you confirm this at the meetings to the gentlemen you met and through this document to all those to whom the document was addressed?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And it goes on to say: "Where no conflicts have emerged to date. Representatives of the HVO Herceg-Bosnia will enable safe passage of all MTS logistics for the 2nd Corps. The MTS acquired in the Republic of Croatia, and Konjuh special purpose production will be delivered to the HVO 107th Brigade allowing for the 2nd Corps to decide on the distribution of the MTS to all of the corps units." Does it follow from this part of your report -- does it confirm what you said about the reasons why all the documents are addressed to the 107th and 108th HVO brigades?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this method of distribution or, rather, this method of sending and distributing the MTS was agreed from the beginning to the end of the war and it was implemented in this way, and with this sentence inserted into our report which was delivered to all the addressees that you saw, we simply confirmed that this was so.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, here we see under B, C, D, and E, that different questions are considered all pertaining to logistics, but anyway, this is what you say was the -- were the conclusions of the meeting; right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, when it comes to conclusion and proposals, are these proposals which emerged from your discussions with the gentlemen you had meetings with?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Under 3(B) it says that joint commands of the armed forces should be established as soon as possible. Was that one of the proposals?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Under (H) it says that the BH Army -- OS of the BH Army and HVO should be engaged to deblock Sarajevo, the corridor towards Orasje, Srebrenica, and axes which the SSVK considers to be of importance. What is SSVK?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: The staff of the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Right. Now it says that the proposals and conclusions are something that the 2nd corps command informed the Tuzla district municipal Presidency about. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that that was done because these were important questions pertaining to their relations, and we would also inform the Presidency of the district.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar from your position and from your letters, we can see that when it came to MTS procurement and assessment and evaluation of what the armed forces and the BH Army should do together with the November, can we then conclude that you had similar positions that you shared with HVO representatives whom you encountered?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: I'd just like to make a correction. These are not my positions. I just conveyed in my reports everything that was agreed upon and which was the HVO's positions and the representative in Mostar and the 2nd Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, in view of the fact that you informed the Presidency of the Municipal Assembly of the Tuzla district, that's why I asked you that. Did the Presidency support these positions, the positions set out here with respect to a joint struggle against a common enemy and so on?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the president of the district, not only did it support these positions, but I went to attend these meetings with the positions of the Presidency of the district and the representatives of the religious communities, the Mufti, in fact, Mufti Lugovic and Mr. Petar Metanovic [phoen] because we would have frequent meetings with the district Presidency, and at those meetings we would be given political guidelines for how we should act militarily. And so it was absolutely clear that the district Presidency held positions which I conveyed to the HVO in Mostar and the feedback mechanism functioned. I would convey the positions from the meetings held.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You said, Mr. Makar, that sometime in March you went to Mostar again; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And now would you take a look at two documents. 2D1106 is the first one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't want to ask any question, but given that this document seems to be very important, I would like to go to point 1(E). You are the drafter of this document, and while reading what you wrote, we have the following impression: It seems to be suggested that all you need be regrouped, all the units from the ABiH that are in Central Bosnia. Those units are leaning towards the HVO and there is risk of a new conflict because you can already imagine that some soldiers have already been kill or wounded. And you seem to suggest that it will be better to go towards a common enemy. You do not mention it, but we can think that these are the Serbs, and you make a proposal, namely, to redeploy three brigades of the ABiH and one brigade of the HVO to unblock Sarajevo. So there is a very fine-tuned analysis of the situation on the ground. According to you, conflicts in Central Bosnia, I would like to know whether you have any information on that. Do you think that there were -- or what were the reasons for those conflicts? Was it conflicts between the local commanders, or do you feel that those conflicts were part of a much wider strategy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Antonetti, Your Honours, I have a very precise opinion about this, and I worked for three years as a scientific advisor of the institute for investigating war documents in Amsterdam, and in my work there I dealt with many of these issues. I consider, and I'm saying this as a soldier myself, we cannot speak of Bosnia-Herzegovina in general terms about the conflict between the HVO and the BH Army, because judging by the location of the conflict viewed territorially, what surface area that was, and judging by the forces involved in the conflict, that is to say brigades and units, it is obvious that this was not the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Now, whether we can characterise this as local conflicts in individual regions, I don't wish to go into that now. However, the fact remains that the zone under the 2nd Corps of the BH Army was an area that was the largest in Bosnia-Herzegovina, larger than any of the other corps, and that numerically the 2nd Corps numbered about 80.000 soldiers, and I include there members of the HVO Brigades. Furthermore, had there not been conflicts in other areas such as Sarajevo, well, I would agree with your assertion, and I, too, think that all this depended on the locality and territory where the conflicts broke out. The second reason is this, and what I can say specifically for the area of defence and territory of the Tuzla district: We cooperated closely with the organs of political power and authority of the districts, municipalities, and as the corps command, we immediately accepted the platform of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina. We had the same views and the political organs and the corps command, shared them. The political situation in the area was such that the forces which were in the majority were those -- well, no conflicts could have emerged from those forces. Now, as far as the political leadership is concerned in the district and the municipality, at the beginning of the war we took over a motto which we applied throughout the war until the end of the war and that was this: That while the war was going on, none of us had the right to any political activities, political action, and that our enemies were only the Chetniks. And when I say the Chetniks, I mean -- and the corps command and the political leadership in the area, well, we always differentiated between the Chetniks and the Serbs. As far as we were concerned, Chetniks were the ones who attacked us, those who attacked us, and those who did not want to live in communality as we had been living up until then. They wished to destroy the values of the life -- the kind of life we led up until then. So that was our sole political goal in fighting, in combat, and that that was the case in some other locations, too, parts of the territory that you mentioned. I do believe that there wouldn't have been any conflicts there had not that been the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, Judge Antonetti showed you point (E) on page 1, and I'd just like you to clarify whether those were your position or were they positions which were put forward by the gentlemen that you talked to in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have not forgotten the question asked by Judge Antonetti. They are not my positions, it is not my position. I write this in my report which was signed by the corps command or, rather, the commander of the corps command, and this report went to the staff of the Supreme Command, and it relates to the proposal made by the individuals I talked to in Mostar; that is to say, men from the HVO who proposed that we undertake a joint operation to deblock Sarajevo which was facing the most critical situation. And we also proposed this: That they set aside one HVO Brigade and that the staff of the Supreme Command should set aside three brigades from the BH Army for that same operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I see. Fine. Now, Mr. Makar, this brings us to your second visit. You said that in March 1993 you went to Mostar for the second time, and I'd like to ask you to look at the following documents, two documents in actual fact, the first of which is 2D1106. May we have your comments? What kind of document is this? What is it about?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is precisely -- this is a permit signed by the commander of the 2nd Corps, Hazim Sadic, and we can see that the deputy commander signed for him, which was normal at that time, giving me permission to go, to travel to Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The next document is 2D1110.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a document and an event which I remember very well. During the discussions, Mr. Bruno Stojic, who signed this, asked where we would spend the night. I don't know what we said, but anyway, he provided accommodation and food at the Citluk hotel in Citluk, and that is what this document confirms.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Before we take a break, Mr. Makar, can you remember and explain to us briefly what was the reason for your second visit? What was the main reason for your second visit?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Well, the main reason was just like on the previous occasion, when I went and when the other officers of the corps went, to secure as much MTS as possible, as much as the HVO could set aside for the 2nd Corps and to ensure free passage to the 2nd Corps zone.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you discuss that during your second visit?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, we did discuss that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before I move on to another area where I need to show three documents in a row, I think that this would be a good time to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I didn't realise, but we need to have a break now. We shall have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall give the floor to Mr. Scott, who would like to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you very much. Mr. President, Your Honours, good afternoon to each of you. Good afternoon to counsel and all those in and around the courtroom. Your Honour, I thought it was appropriate to just to take one minute of the Chamber's time, just as I listen to the testimony of this witness today and other witnesses over the past several weeks to remind the Chamber of a position that the Prosecution has repeatedly stated. And I did pull up, in one particular instance, this is a statement that we made on the 5th of April, 2007, during the testimony of Mr. Okun, and it's at transcript page 16978, lest anyone wants to check me on it. Transcript 16978, and I say at the time on these issues about providing arms to various units and operations in Bosnia and Herzegovina: "In the course of the war from 1991 to 1995 there were any number of places where indeed the Croats and the Muslims were fighting together against the Serbs both in 1991 and 1992. Again in 1994 and 1995, and indeed in some places even in 1993 while they were fighting each other they were also fighting together against the Serbs in various parts of Bosnia." Now, that's been the Prosecution's position since this case started. This is one place where we cited on the 5th of April, 2007, almost two years ago. So as we seem to be spending an awful lot of time, especially in a situation where we're frequently told that the Defence don't have enough time to present their cases, that there isn't enough time to present the Defence case, we're spending an awful lot of time on matters that are not in dispute. No one has ever said -- the Prosecution has never said that arms were not provided by the Croats, the Bosnian Croats, to fight the common enemy the Serbs in the area of Tuzla. That has never been disputed, but apparently we've spent the last two or three hours proving something that's never been in dispute, as we said on a number of occasions, including on the 5th of April, 2007. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's bring the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may respond very briefly. I'm glad my learned friend brought this up, but this has to do not only with supplies of weapons but also other issues. The Defence is putting forward evidence showing that the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, in certain areas of Bosnia-Herzegovina, had direct command over particular HVO units which were part of the HZ HB, and we showed this using both the example of Posavina and the example of Sarajevo, and now through this witness we are doing the same using the 2nd Corps as an example. I think this is highly significant, and I will continue my examination-in-chief because this does deal not -- this deals not just with supplies of weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, you said that in late April or early May you visited Mostar again. Can you explain to Their Honours with whom you met in Mostar and what happened in the course of your third visit?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: My third visit was connected exclusively to the very difficult situation. There were fierce attacks in the area of the 2nd Corps, and we had a great need for MTS. So that was the main task I had when going to Mostar. I spoke to Mr. Stojic, Mr. Praljak, the same men I've already mentioned, Mr. Petkovic and Mr. Rajic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, please look at 2D1107 now.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Excuse me -- sorry. Yes, here it is. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you clarify to Their Honours? This is a safe conduct pass. It also mentions your name. Can you tell us from whom you received this MTS and whether it was for the needs of the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can confirm that this was MTS which I received from the HVO in Mostar and which I brought to Tuzla, but I had a lot of problems along the way.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, can we now look at 2D1108.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. This document is linked to the previous document. It's the dispatch notes for the MTS which I took and brought to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The date is the 1st of May, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, can you confirm to Their Honours -- or, rather, tell them the following: Do you know whether the MTS mentioned in these notes we have shown so far sent to the 2nd Corps, whether it was paid for?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Excuse me, are you referring to the MTS mentioned in the last two documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: My question is general. The MTS that you took delivery of, was it paid for?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: No, it was not paid for.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, do you know whether the MTS obtained directly from the Ministry of Defence in Zagreb were paid for in full?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the MTS I said had been received from the Ministry of Defence were paid for only in part, but in part they were sent without payment.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, before we move on to a new topic, can you confirm, based on all these notes we've seen today which reached the 2nd Corps by various methods, can you confirm whether this MTS actually reached the 2nd Corps of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I can, because I was at the head of the staff which, due to combat activities in the corps for which it was most responsible, had to know what MTS had arrived and how to distribute it. I was therefore authorised by the corps commander to monitor, together with the logistics organs, everything that arrived in the corps and how it was distributed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, besides these supplies procured for the 2nd Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO units subordinated to the 2nd Corps in Tuzla, did anyone else provide MTS for your needs?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've already stated in my reply to the question as to how we obtained MTS, that this was done through a rather large number of people. In addition to the people in the logistics centre in Zagreb and some officers primarily from the logistics of the 2nd Corps, these people went off to obtain MTS. We also had a special assistant who was the corps commander for procurement whom I've already mentioned. This was Mr. Edin Delibegovic. He procured most of the MTS.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar let's look at 2D1077 now. Can you tell Their Honours the following. This is a table showing MTS purchased.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: On page 2, Your Honours, I see the name of Fadil Muhic. I know Fadil Muhic very well. We still see a lot of each other after the war. He was in that logistics centre in Zagreb, and as far as I can see this document shows that this is actually a report by Fadil Muhic about all the MTS purchased for the 107th Gradacac Brigade in October 1992 up to December 1993, and in the title it says, "... bought and forwarded to the brigade." I saw such reports during the war. This was MTS which arrived in the corps and was then distributed to where it was most needed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, let's look at 2D1078 now. This is a financial report --

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. Concerning the procurement of the MTS for the needs of the 2nd Corps. And on page 3 it says, Assistant Commander Edin Delibegovic. I've already mentioned him. Evidently this is a report about how he as an assistant for procurement spent the funds he had available to procure weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, before your testimony here, did you have occasion to learn anything about this purchase of MTS?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. I knew about the purchase of this MTS. I also knew about some of the ways in which funds were obtained, but I'd like to draw attention to the following here: There's an error on page 3. It says "Tuzla, 12th of December, 1992," but I can see from the text that this materiel was obtained in 1993. So obviously this is an error. He is submitting a report in February 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now that we're on page 3, does it follow from this that this MTS was procured from the Republic of Croatia? Was it obtained there? Look at the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. From the preceding text and especially the passage you pointed out, it's evident that the MTS was obtained through the assistant minister of the Republic of Croatia, of the minister of defence, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It says here that this -- the payments will be dealt with at the level of the two republics. Does this refer to the Republic of Croatia and the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: This follows not only from this document, but that's how it was. Very often, as we did not have funds available, we would deliver salt from the Tuzla salt factory, and very often from Sarajevo we received requests for certain quantities of salt to be sent in lieu of payment due, payments due.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: There are a number of attachments mentioned to this document. I'll read them out and just tell me whether these are the documents referred to here. It's 2D1079, please.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. Evidently this document shows part of the MTS mentioned in this financial section.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The next document is 2D1080.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I confirm that that is also part of this report.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. This too. You can see that Mr. Delibegovic took delivery of the MTS.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, this too.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. And it says here in what amount the MTS has been paid for.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: This document shows what MTS was obtained and how much has been paid for.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: 2D1089 [as interpreted]. Is this a final summary, an overview? 2D1098 is the right number.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is evidently a document providing an overview, and it shows what has been paid for and the various segments are mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: 2D1097 finally.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Well, this is not really legible.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This document was signed by Mr. Delibegovic on the 8th of March, and he refers to the MTS mentioned in document 2D1078. And I wish to draw your attention to item 2 where it says: "The materiel was purchased from the end of August, 1992 until February 1993. Practically this is a large quantity of MTS, one of the largest quantities obtained for the needs of the 2nd Corps. "The transport of MTS was organised 11 times, and most of the MTS was brought to this area." It says that: "Goods are sometimes held up in Grude or Kiseljak, but all these purchases and transport were organised by me with the consent of the commander of the 2nd Corps." My question is: Is it evident from this document that this MTS was purchased from the end of August 1992, until February 1993, and as Mr. Delibegovic says, this -- these goods, almost all of them reached the area, and we'll deal with the problems later on.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. This document confirms the time-frame, but I wish to make a correction to what you said. It should say practically this is a great majority of the MTS. This was most of the MTS that ever reached the 2nd Corps. And it says that there were 11 transports, and the summary we have just seen is attached to this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, did the 2nd Corps ever obtain any other MTS arriving from the logistics centres of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There was MTS coming from the logistics centres of the ABiH and from the logistics centres of various brigades and various municipalities had their logistics centres in Zagreb. Part of this MTS was donated and part of it was allocated.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's look at 2D1099. Can you explain to Their Honours what this is about?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I remember this document very well, because it deals with a special case. This refers to the donation of a large amount of communications equipment. It was donated by a company from Liechtenstein, and it was sent through the BH Army logistics centre in Zagreb with a final destination Tuzla and Gradacac, and it was sent to Mr. Zeljko Knez, the commander of the 2nd Corps of the ABiH, and Mr. Ivan Miocevic, and I know the signature of Muradif Pajt, because I sent my own communications chief to Zagreb to take delivery of this equipment.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, do you recall whether any MTS was obtained for the needs of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina when there were offensives going on on the territory of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina launched by the Yugoslav Army and the Serbian units in March and April 1993?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: I've already mentioned that such offensives and fierce fighting on the territory of the 2nd Corps were practically ongoing, continuous throughout the war, and there was a fierce attack in the area of defence of the 2nd Corps, and we needed fresh MTS, which was the reason I visited Mostar for the third time, as I've already explained, when I brought back a large quantity of MTS. At the time, this MTS saved the situation, which was very critical. I know that there were huge problems during the offensive conducted in the area of Srebrenica and that considerable amounts of MTS were required.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you now look at 2D1100. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no English translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. We did not have an interpretation, and I think there is another microphone on in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you repeat what you said after you saw document 2D1100? Can you repeat your answer, please?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is clearly evident from this document that the HVO approved safe conduct and a considerable quantity of MTS - when I say "considerable quantity," I'm referring to the amounts I see in this document - to be sent to Srebrenica, because it says that the materials are to be transported on the Grude-Srebrenica route, and the details of the trucks are listed. The date is the 7th of April, 1993, which is when the situation in that area was critical.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, can you confirm that this MTS was received by the 2nd Corps as you know that this was a difficult period in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Well, we monitored that part of the war theatre closely at the time, and in spite of our physical distance, we had constant communication with them. So I do know that this MTS arrived at its destination.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, we spoke about the problems -- or, rather, we mentioned that there were some problems as seen in previous documents in the transports of this MTS to Tuzla. At the time that you went to bring back MTS, and also when others brought the MTS to its destination, were there any problems and, if so, what were the problems.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I could speak about that at length, but probably time would not allow that. I myself had problems on the road when I was leading individual convoys, but in conclusion I can say that the problems stemmed, and I can say this as a military expert, from the fact that in this war a firm military organisation had not yet been established in which lower-ranking commanders have to obey orders coming from high er-ranking commanders without fail. Very often local commanders, both in the HVO and the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, would sometimes hold up convoys or even confiscate some MTS from the convoys which passed through.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could we now look at 2D1116. And this is letter from the HVO Mostar Defence Department to Mr. Bruno Stojic in person sent by Mr. Sadic, and here he discusses these problems and speaks of the needs of the 2nd Corps and their other logistical needs; right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document, looking at the date which is the 4th of March, 1993, is the result of a discussion I had with the HVO in Mostar during my first visit there, which was in February. At the time, we had agreed on the communication and that we should have communication between ourselves talking about problems linked -- problems occurring on a local level with respect to MTS, whichever side experienced them. And so my commander in war, Mr. Hazim Sadic, sent to Mr. Bruno Stojic, as I see here, sent him information and reports about the problems for us to be able to solve them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, in point 6 of this document, as you've just said, Mr. Sadic is suggesting to Mr. Stojic that he send in his requests and state his problems so that they could be solved. Now, my question to you is this: To the best of your knowledge, the problems that occurred with respect to transport, were they solved?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can confirm that the problems were solved on the basis of agreement either in writing, as the case was here, and communication was two-way, and the problems would be solved sometimes by picking up the phone, on the phone if something was urgent, through the communications links.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now let's look at 2D1101, the next document, please. This is a letter from Mr. Sefer Halilovic, with the same date, referring to the previous letter, which was document 2D1116, and here we have -- well, it says the command of the 4th Corps, and it says that Arif Pasalic, the commander of the 4th Corps, confirms this. Now, can you explain why there are two stamps on this letter from Mr. Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, yes, I can explain that. This document, 1116, the one we looked at previously, was sent to the Supreme Command Staff, to Mr. Sefer Halilovic as well, and after that he sent a letter of his own to the Croatian Defence Council, Mostar, to Mr. Bruno Stojic and Mr. Milivoj Petkovic. Now, for reasons of military organisation and the communications systems organisation, the Supreme Command Staff communicated with the command of the 4th Corps in Mostar. And it's quite obvious that this letter reached the 4th Corps command and that at the bottom there we have the signature of the commander of the 4th Corps, Mr. Arif Pasalic, and that he was given the assignment and carried it out of sending the letter to the HVO of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What is important in this document, and I'd like to draw your attention to that, is paragraph 3 where Mr. Sefer Halilovic says as follows: "I would also like to take this opportunity to ask you if you have any type of ammunition and other MTS, especially artillery ammunition and POB ..." Will you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Anti-armour combat is POB.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: "To lend them to us or give them to us, and we will remunerate you -- or, rather, in exchange for financial cooperation." And then in the next paragraph -- or, rather, in the previous paragraph he deals with the situation in Srebrenica. He says: "Please grant all the requests stated in Mr. Sadic's letter as soon as possible because the fate of more than 60.000 people in the free territory of Srebrenica depends on this." Now, Mr. Sefer Halilovic refers to the common foe, common enemy. The document is dated the 4th of March, 1993. And now, Mr. Makar, we have seen the document. It will come up on your screen again. It is 2D1100 of the 7th of April, 1993, when you said that the Main Staff gave permission for resources for Srebrenica, because we can see quite obviously that in April 1993 the Main Staff, in reacting to these demands, permitted the resources to go to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes. The document has just come up on the screen. We've already discussed it, and looking at the date I think it is obvious that it was a reaction from the Main Staff of the HVO to the request made by Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, you discussed the problems that occurred in Bosnia-Herzegovina accompanying the transport of these convoys and passage of the convoys. Let's look at a joint document now. It is 2D1037, and they are problems which occurred in territory controlled by the BH Army. This is a piece of information from the Security Sector of the Defence Department, and I'm going to ask you about some of the facts stipulated in this report, whether you know of them. This is a document dated the 30th of January, 1993, and it speaks of 54 trucks, materiel which at the end of November and beginning of December for the requirements of the 107th HVO Brigade of Gradacac set out from Zagreb. From this document, and let me just tell you briefly about this, but anyway, it emerges and follows that 30 trucks never arrived in Gradacac and that the information that the person received, the person was called Ivan Roso, according to what he learned, the information he received, those trucks allegedly were unloaded in the logistics base in Visoko. Now, Mr. Makar, at the end it says what quantities -- the quantities concerned. Now, do you know -- on the third page it says 30 trucks were certainly unloaded in the logistics centre of the BH Army in Visoko, and most probably they were distributed to the units of the BH Army in the field. Now, did you -- and the source of this information here is Mr. Zeljko Knez. Do you know what things like this happened, that is to say, that the MTS that was sent for the requirements of the 2nd Corps somehow turned up at the logistics centre in Visoko where they were then distributed to any unit of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I remember this case very well, because it was January 1993, which was the time that I spent in the Gradacac area where fierce fighting was going on, and that the Chetniks threatened to enter the town of Gradacac. So the situation was very critical, especially with respect to the MTS situation, and we were expecting this particular convoy to arrive. Now, when less than half the convoy arrived, I remember that I contacted the commander, who was Mr. Zeljko Knez at the time, and asked him what had happened to the rest. I don't know what was done, but anyway, later on I also learnt that that part of the convoy had probably ended up in the logistics centre of the BH Army in Visoko.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, I'm going to show you a few documents now which refer to a convoy that we can call the double-bottom convoy to be able to identify it better. So we'll call it that will provisionally. I'm going to show you the documents. I know that you were involved in this, but perhaps before you see the documents you could explain to the Trial Chamber what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document tells me about something that I was very familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Just a moment. Well, then I'll give you the number of the document. 2D1112 is the number. Are you looking at that document?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: No, I'm not. I beg your pardon. Yes, I've found it now, 1112.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Now you can continue and tell us what you know about it.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: It is a permit to Mr. Avdo Mesic to go and fetch some resources for the 2nd Corps, and the date is 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Now did you comment on 2D1113, the next document?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that is a document which follows this first one and refers to the individuals who will go with Mr. Avdo Mesic to procure MTS.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, now look at 2D1114, the next document, which is a report, but before we comment on that report, can you briefly tell the Trial Chamber what happened when Mr. Mesic, Avdo Mesic, went pursuant to these permits?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
