utterances.text: Your Honours, I've already said that on the basis of an agreement with the HVO in Mostar, we had a very proper relationship in that we endeavoured to adhere to what we had agreed upon. Now, in this particular case, Mr. Mesic, Mr. Avdo Mesic, whom I personally know, engaged in some improper acts -- or, rather, he made a double-bottom to a truck, a false bottom, and in that false bottom he tried to transport some MTS that had not been listed on the authorised list. As far as I know, at certain check-points along the way in the area under the control of the HVO of Mostar, those trucks were stopped and searched, and they found what was happening, and so that's the problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Trial Chamber who compiled this report and on what occasion?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: This is Mr. Avdo Mesic's report upon his return to Tuzla, because most probably the corps command asked for a report, because certain acts had been committed which had violated the agreement. And so Mr. Mesic has written a long report reporting on the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, were you personally informed about what had happened with this convoy and with that false bottom or double-bottom?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I was informed about that. I learnt about the incident when it happened, and the commander charged me with going to deal with the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's look at 2D1115 now, please, which is the next document. And my question to you is this: Did some organs conduct an investigation into this incident and were the facts established as to how this came about?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this, as far as I can see, well, there's no heading there so we don't see who compiled the report and there's no signature either, but in general terms this could have been a report from our security organs, and the commander had probably given them the assignment of investigating the matter concerning Mr. Mesic's convoy and checking out the facts from the report that he had sent in. As far as I can see, at the end of this report it was addressed to the Municipal Assembly of Tuzla, Mr. Selim Beslagic; the Tuzla district, Mr. Esad Hadzic; the security organs, one copy, of course; and another copy to the Chief of Staff. That is to say, it reached me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Makar, you can in fact confirm that you received this report, a copy of it?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Not to dwell on the details, but it follows from this report that Mr. Avdo Mesic, without permission from the 2nd Corps, attempted, along with the MTS that had been approved, to bring in certain MTS that had not been approved; right?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Well, from this report that I received from the security organs that would be the conclusion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Just two details. On page 2, under number 12 it says: "In view of this problem, the Chief of Staff of the 2nd Corps has been called to Mostar, Mr. Andjelko Makar, who along with great efforts managed to put the mistakes right, and we managed to procure --" That's on page 2.

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: "He managed to smooth over the mistakes made Avdo Mesic, and we purchased significant quantities of MTS for the 2nd Corps which were brought to Tuzla with regular documentation and no problems." And your name is mentioned here. So does that refer to your trips to Mostar and the MTS quantities that you procured for the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: ANDJELKO MAKAR
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that. I can confirm that I was in Mostar. I did go to Mostar, and on route I met part of the convoy that had been allowed to pass through because it had all the rights papers and there was no problem. And in talking to the people in Mostar, I managed to secure, as it says here, considerable quantities of MTS.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since it's exactly 7.00 now, can we adjourn for the day, and then I'll see how much time I have left and continue tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have about 18 minutes left. So as you know, we shall resume tomorrow at 14.30. So we'll start 15 minutes late. Witness, until tomorrow, please have no contact whatsoever with anyone regarding your testimony here, and we will have the pleasure to see you again tomorrow at 2.30. I wish everyone a good evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 24th day of March, 2009, at 2.30 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
